Bewerbergemeinschaften haben eine von allen Mitgliedern unterzeichnete Erklärung abzu- geben, in welcher sie die Aufgabenteilung innerhalb der Bewerbergemeinschaft darstellen, einen bevollmächtigten Vertreter der Bewerbergemeinschaft benennen und erklären, dass L-Bank Europaweite Vergabe einer KI-gestützten Lösung zur Verarbei- tung von Elterngeldanträgen und Nachweisen Seite 11 von 20 Seiten vertraulich alle Mitglieder der Bewerbergemeinschaft im Vergabeverfahren sowie im Auftragsfall ge- samtschuldnerisch haften. 3.4 Eignungsleihe / Unterauftragnehmer Ein Bewerber kann zum Nachweis seiner Eignung (wirtschaftliche und finanzielle sowie technische und berufliche Leistungsfähigkeit) die Kapazitäten anderer Unternehmen in An- spruch nehmen (Eignungsleihe). Diese Möglichkeit besteht unabhängig von der Rechtsna- tur der zwischen dem Bewerber und den anderen Unternehmen bestehenden Verbindun- gen. In diesem Fall ist der Vergabestelle nachzuweisen, dass dem Bewerber die erforderli- chen Mittel tatsächlich zur Verfügung stehen werden, indem beispielsweise eine entspre- chende Verpflichtungserklärung dieses Unternehmens vorgelegt wird. Die Unternehmen, auf die sich ein Bewerber zum Nachweis seiner Eignung stützt, müssen die Eignung hinsichtlich derjenigen Eignungskriterien erfüllen, zu deren Nachweis sich der Bewerber auf die Eignung des Unternehmens stützt. Zudem sind die Erklärungen über das Vorliegen von Ausschlussgründen nach § 123 Abs. 1 bis 4 GWB und § 124 Abs. 1 GWB auch für diese Unternehmen vorzulegen. Werden die vorstehend dargestellten Eignungs- anforderungen nicht erfüllt oder liegen Ausschlussgründe gemäß § 123 Abs. 1 bis 4 GWB vor, so ist das Unternehmen auf Aufforderung der Vergabestelle innerhalb einer von dieser vorgegeb

NATIONAL INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY AUTHORITY – UGANDA (NITA-U)

 

 REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION

UGANDA DIGITAL ACCELERATION PROJECT – GOVERNMENT NETWORK (UDAP-GOVNET)

PROJECT ID: P171305

LOAN NUMBER: IDA-68980

 

REFERENCE NUMBER: NITA-UDAP/CONS/26-27/00027

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE: CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE NATIONAL DIGITAL SKILLS TRAINING PROGRAMME (NDSTP)

 

The Government of Uganda, represented by the National Information Technology Authority – Uganda (NITA-U), has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Uganda Digital Acceleration Project – Government Network (UDAP-GOVNET) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consultancy services for the implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP)

 

The con

responsibility of implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP) programme across Uganda. The assignment will equip at least 6,000 beneficiaries drawn from public servants, teachers and tutors, out-of-school youth, refugees and refugee-host communities, and persons with disabilities with the digital knowledge and practical competencies needed to access services safely and productively, pursue education and livelihood opportunities, and participate as informed digital citizens.

The duration of the assignment will be five (5) months from the date of contract signing.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be accessed at https://www.nita.go.ug

The National Information Technology Authority - Uganda now invites eligible consulting firms to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria for the firm’s capability and experience is:

 

The shortlisting criteria for the firm’s capacity and experience are:

insurance_bonds.text: EMENT OF OBJECTIVES (SOO) For Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) Topic Area 3 1.0 Purpose The objective of this effort is to address cyber threats to national critical space missions (e.g., Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT), Missile Warning/Missile Tracking (MW/MT), Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM)) through the research, design, development, testing, and demonstration of a comprehensive Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) system. 2.0 Background Space vehicles are increasingly recognized as vulnerable platforms facing sophisticated cyber threats. To ensure mission assurance, there is a critical need to provide advanced defensive solutions for space assets. This project aims to reduce the attack surfaces of space vehicles and implement robust resiliency mechanisms that enable self-protection and rapid recovery from cyber anomalies, leveraging Cyber-Hardened Satellite Software (CHSS) technology. 3.0 Period and Place of Performance • Period of Performance: The anticipated period of performance is a 12-month Base effort, followed by three (3) 12-month Option periods, plus 3 months for final reporting (Total 51 Months). • Place of Performance: The work will be performed primarily at the contractors facilit

C.1.1 Eligibility: To be eligible to participate in the medical plan, LE Staff (both full time and part time) must be: -- Paid under the terms of the Local Compensation Plan (LCP); and – -- Under a non-temporary direct hire appointment, personal services agreement (PSA), or personal services contract (PSC); or -- Under a temporary direct hire appointment or PSA Fixed Term of one year or more. Not eligible are those working under temporary appointments; those working under a PSC or PSA that is time limited to less than one year; non-personal services contract personnel and their employees, supplied by an independent contractor l

C.1.2 Riders: There are no riders under this contract. C.1.3 Periods of Ineligibility: Employees and their dependents are not entitled to health benefits during any period of employment for which premiums are not paid. Additionally, employee's dependents are not entitled to health benefits during any period of employment during which the employee was not eligible to participate. During a period of extended Leave Without Pay (LWOP) or other unpaid leave beyond one pay period, the employee is responsible for the full cost of the insurance premiums for self and dependents. The Mission will pay the premiums directly to the Contractor and will collect the full cost from the employee on a quarterly basis. Alternatively

LE: files/Attach_1_-_Blood_Transfusion_Services_SOW.pdf ===== Statement of Work For Transfusion Services 20 October 2026 I. Background: The 88th Medical Group Transfusion Services requires blood components and references lab transfusion testing services. The supplier shall provide blood products and reference blood transfusion services (testing) to support the blood supply in case of emergency situations and inpatient and outpatient care at the WPAFB Medical Center when requested for a period of 5 years at the prices in the approved price list. II. Minimum Technical Requirements: The supplier shall provide blood products and reference transfusion testing that are time dependent with immediate response and expedience to treat critical patients. The supplier must operate 24/7 as the 88th Medical Group (MDG) is a 24/7 operation; this service must be available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, including holidays and weekends. The supplier shall provide rapid shipment of blood products when the 88 MDG Transfusion Services in-house inventory is in need to support critical patients. The one-hour turnaround time for testing is a mission-critical requirement. The blood supplier shall deliver routine blood products ordered on a STAT basis within one (1) hour of the blood sup

eipt of an emergent request for blood products. The required completion point is delivery to the Transfusion Services department. The supplier must fulfill our request with the ordered product with appropriate compatible blood type, applicable testing, and requested quantities. Any unforeseen delays are understandable; however, the ultimate goal is for the delivering agency to aim for the <1 hour delivery time. An appropriate transmittal list is required with each delivery. If emergent requests are unable to be consistently met, it could mean critical failure for our hospital's life-saving capabilities. The supplier shall have 24/7 reference laboratory testing capabilities for patients anticipating transfusions or medical treatment. The supplier must be licensed by the Food & Drug Administration (FDA) and follow American Association of Blood Bank (AABB) standards. The supplier must notify the 88th MDG Transfusion Services of all unexpected/abnormal tests from blood products supplied by them. The supplier shall provide look-back notifications to the 88th MDG as required by 21 CFR 610.48 (b)(3): (a) within three (3) calendar days if blood collected from a donor who tested negative at the time of donation but tests reactive for evidence of HIV or HCV infection on a later do
